chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying to Abu Baseer: 'But, by Allah! If I were to find three Momineen from among you who are concealing my hadith, I would not have considered it permissible that I should be concealing a single hadith from them.'

key_terms.أَكْتُمَهُمْ: conceal from them — withhold or hide knowledge from the believers
key_terms.اسْتَحْلَلْتُ: considered it permissible — deemed it religiously lawful or acceptable
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ: three — the minimum number of trustworthy believers the Imam sought as a condition for full disclosure
key_terms.حَدِيثِي: my hadith — the Imam's narrations, rulings, and transmitted sacred knowledge
key_terms.مُؤْمِنِينَ: Momineen — true believers characterized by sound faith and trustworthiness worthy of receiving the Imam's knowledge
key_terms.يَكْتُمُونَ: concealing — faithfully guarding and keeping secret the Imam's narrations from those unworthy of them

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say he would not withhold any hadith if he found three trustworthy Momineen?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdullah Ja'far al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) expresses to Abu Baseer his profound desire to transmit his knowledge fully to trustworthy believers, declaring that if he could find even three Momineen who faithfully guard his hadith, he would deem it impermissible to withhold a single narration from them. The hadith highlights the Imam's eagerness to share sacred knowledge and his grief over the acute scarcity of truly trustworthy followers capable of preserving it. It establishes trustworthiness and discretion as essential prerequisites for receiving the Imam's complete teachings.
